He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Campbell Fighting Camels basketball|Campbell Fighting Camels]]. ==Early life== Growing up in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]], Clemons idolized [[Allen Iverson]] and sought to incorporate Iverson's crossover dribble into his playing style. Despite standing 5'9, Clemons could dunk in high school at [[Millbrook High School (North Carolina)|Millbrook]]. Campbell coach [[Kevin McGeehan]] recruited him due to his confidence and 44-inch vertical leap.{{cite news |last1=Forgrave |first1=Reid |title=The nation's leading returning scorer may be small, but has big dream of NBA Draft |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/the-nations-leading-returning-scorer-may-be-small-but-has-big-dream-of-nba-draft/ |access-date=June 6, 2018 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=October 7, 2017}} In a state tournament game as a senior, Clemons broke the school single-game record with 41 points.{{cite news |last1=Schafer |first1=Josh |title=Campbell's 5-foot-9 guard Chris Clemons is among the nation's top scorers |url=http://dailyorange.com/2017/02/campbells-5-foot-9-guard-chris-clemons-is-among-the-nations-top-scorers/ |access-date=June 5, 2018 |work=The Daily Orange |date=March 2, 2018}} ==College career== Clemons averaged 18.5 points per game as a freshman at Campbell and was named the Big South Freshman of the Year. Shooting 18-of-32 from the field, Clemons scored 51 points in an 81–79 win over [[UNC Asheville Bulldogs men's basketball|UNC Asheville]] in the Big South Tournament as a sophomore, breaking the tournament scoring record. He became the fourth player to score 50 points that season.{{cite news |last1=Payne |first1=Terrence |title=Campbell's Chris Clemons scores 51 in quarterfinal upset |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2017/03/02/campbells-chris-clemons-scores-51-in-quarterfinal-upset/ |access-date=June 5, 2018 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=March 2, 2017}} Clemons was named to the First Team All-Big South in his sophomore season.{{cite press release|url=http://bigsouthsports.com/news/2017/2/27/MBB_0227173359.aspx |title=Big South Announces 2016–17 Men's Basketball Award Winners |publisher=Big South Conference |date=February 27, 2017 |access-date=February 27, 2017}} As a sophomore, Clemons averaged 25.1 points per game, second highest in Division I behind [[Marcus Keene]], and took 42.2 percent of his team's shots, the highest percentage in college basketball. With 904 points, Clemons set the school record for points in a season.{{cite news |last1=Pope |first1=Jonas |title=Former Millbrook star Chris Clemons withdraws from NBA draft, heads back to Campbell |url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/article212214139.html |access-date=June 5, 2018 |work=[[The News & Observer]] |date=May 30, 2018}} Clemons had a season-high 42 points against [[Liberty Flames men's basketball|Liberty]] on January 23, 2018, and alongside [[Marcus Burk]] became the first teammates in NCAA history to each hit 10 threes in a game.{{cite news |last1=Fuchs |first1=Jeremy |title=Top Scorer and 5'9" Campbell Guard Chris Clemons Is Out to Prove Himself |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/02/13/campbell-chris-clemons-guard-team-leader-nba-draft |access-date=June 5, 2018 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=February 13, 2018}} He passed the 2,000 point mark in his career on February 7, scoring 33 points in a win against [[Gardner–Webb Runnin' Bulldogs men's basketball|Gardner–Webb]].{{cite news|title=Clemons scores 2,000th point in Campbell victory|url=http://www.fayobserver.com/sports/20180207/clemons-scores-2000th-point-in-campbell-victory|access-date=February 10, 2018|work=[[The Fayetteville Observer]]|date=February 7, 2018}} On March 14, Clemons passed [[Jonathan Rodriguez (basketball)|Jonathan Rodriguez]] as Campbell's all-time leading scorer, adding 32 points in a win against [[Miami RedHawks men's basketball|Miami (Ohio)]].{{cite news |last1=Newkirk |first1=Sam |title=Time to go pro? Campbell basketball star Chris Clemons announces his plans |url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/article205223354.html |access-date=June 5, 2018 |work=[[The News & Observer]] |date=March 15, 2018}} Clemons repeated on the First Team All-Big South as a junior and received seven first place votes for conference player of the year.{{cite press release|url=http://bigsouthsports.com/news/2018/2/26/big-south-announces-2017-18-mens-basketball-award-winners.aspx |title=Big South Announces 2017–18 Men's Basketball Award Winners |publisher=Big South Conference |date=February 26, 2018 |access-date=February 26, 2018}} As a junior, Clemons averaged 24.9 points per game, fourth highest in the nation. He helped the Camels go 18–16 and play in the [[College Basketball Invitational]]. After the season, Clemons declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] but did not hire an agent, thus preserving his collegiate eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Blake |first1=J. Mike |title=Time to go pro? Campbell basketball star Chris Clemons announces his plans |url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/article207810629.html |access-date=June 5, 2018 |work=[[The News & Observer]] |date=April 3, 2018}} He decided to withdraw from the draft and return to Campbell. Coming into his senior season, Clemons was named Preseason Big South Player of the Year.{{cite web |title=Big South Announces 2018–19 Men's Basketball Preseason Awards |url=http://bigsouthsports.com/news/2018/10/20/big-south-announces-2018-19-mens-basketball-preseason-awards.aspx |website=Big South Conference |access-date=October 24, 2018 |date=October 20, 2018}} On December 21, 2018, Clemons became the all-time leading scorer in Big South history. He passed [[VMI Keydets basketball|VMI]] guard [[Reggie Williams (basketball, born 1986)|Reggie Williams]]' 2,556 career point total in a game against [[Austin Peay Governors men's basketball|Austin Peay]].{{cite news|url=https://bigsouthsports.com/news/2018/12/22/mens-basketball-chris-clemons-becomes-big-souths-all-time-scorer.aspx|title=Chris Clemons Becomes Big South's All-Time Scorer|first=Jim|last=Allen |website=[[Big South Conference]] |date=December 22, 2018 |access-date=January 8, 2019}} He led NCAA Division 1 in scoring with 30.1 points per game and became the third highest scorer in college basketball history. ==Professional career== ===Houston Rockets (2019–2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]], Clemons joined the [[Houston Rockets]] for the [[2019 NBA Summer League]], and later signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the Rockets.{{cite web|title=Roster Update: Rockets GM Daryl Morey announced today the team has signed rookie free agent guards Chris Clemons, Shamorie Ponds and William McDowell-White. All three players will represent the Rockets at NBA Summer League 2019, which begins on Friday.|url=https://twitter.com/HoustonRockets/status/1146610315460788226|website=Houston Rockets on Twitter|access-date=September 3, 2019|date=July 4, 2019}} On October 17, the Rockets converted him to a two-way player.{{Cite web|url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2019/10/17/houston-rockets-convert-rookie-chris-clemons-to-two-way-contract/|title=Houston Rockets convert rookie Chris Clemons to two-way contract|website=USA Today|date=October 17, 2019|access-date=October 21, 2019}} Clemons made his NBA debut on November 3, scoring 16 points in a 129–100 loss to the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite news |last1=Baxley |first1=Rodd |title=Campbell's Chris Clemons scores 16 in NBA debut |url=https://www.fayobserver.com/sports/20191104/campbells-chris-clemons-scores-16-in-nba-debut |access-date=November 4, 2019 |work=[[Fayetteville Observer]] |date=November 4, 2019}} On November 16, with [[Russell Westbrook]] and [[Eric Gordon]] sidelined due to injury, Clemons scored a career-high 19 points in a win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite news |last1=DuBose |first1=Ben |title=Campbell University retires jersey of Rockets rookie Chris Clemons |url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2020/02/16/campbell-university-retires-jersey-of-rockets-rookie-chris-clemons/ |access-date=February 22, 2020 |work=Rockets Wire |date=February 16, 2020}} On December 27, the [[Houston Rockets]] announced that they had converted the contract with Clemons into standard NBA contract.{{cite web|title=Rockets Convert Contract of Chris Clemons|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-convert-contract-chris-clemons|date=December 27, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 27, 2019}} Clemons recorded 14 points and three rebounds on January 10, 2020, in a 113–92 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite news |title=Rockets' Chris Clemons: Scores 14 points in loss |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/rockets-chris-clemons-scores-14-points-in-loss/ |access-date=January 26, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 10, 2020}} Clemons had his jersey retired at Campbell during the NBA All-Star Break. On December 15, 2020, in a preseason game against the San Antonio Spurs, Clemons tore his Achilles while on defense.{{cite news |last1=DuBose |first1=Ben |title=Rockets expect to lose Chris Clemons for season to torn Achilles|url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2020/12/15/rockets-expect-to-lose-chris-clemons-for-season-to-torn-achilles/ |access-date=December 15, 2020 |work=Rockets Wire |date=December 15, 2020}} On January 21, 2021, he was waived by the Rockets.{{cite web|title=Rockets Acquire Kevin Porter Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-acquire-kevin-porter-jr|date=January 22, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 23, 2021}} ===Maine Celtics (2021–2022)=== On October 16, 2021, Clemons signed with the [[Boston Celtics]],{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Celtics Sign Luke Kornet, Chris Clemons To Camp Deals|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/10/celtics-sign-luke-kornet-chris-clemons-to-camp-deals.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} but was waived soon thereafter.{{cite tweet|author=Keith Smith|number=1449501516344266752|title=Official Boston Celtics waivers: Chris Clemons Luke Kornet Garrison Mathews Theo Pinson Boston now has 16 players under contract. 15 standard deals, 1 Two-Way deal. One Two-Way spot remains open for the Celtics.|user=KeithSmithNBA|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} On October 23, he signed with the [[Maine Celtics]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web|title=Celtics Acquire Two In Draft, Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/draft-camp-102321/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} Clemons averaged 16.3 points, 4.9 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 1.1 steals per game. On December 29, 2021, Clemons signed a 10-day contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-sign-chris-clemons-and-cameron-oliver-10-day-contracts |title=Hawks Sign Chris Clemons and Cameron Oliver to 10-Day Contracts |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 29, 2021 |date=December 29, 2021}} However, he did not appear in a game for Atlanta. On January 8, 2022, Clemons was reacquired by the [[Maine Celtics]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021–22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 8, 2022|access-date=January 8, 2022}} On January 22, 2022, Clemons set an [[NBA G League]] record for most points in a quarter on perfect shooting from the field with 27 points on 9–9 field goal shooting.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/breaking-down-nik-stauskas-wild-57-point-performance|title=Breaking Down Nik Stauskas' Wild Two-Game Stretch|accessdate=May 7, 2022|date=March 3, 2022|work=[[NBA.com]]}} Later that season he would win the G League Player of the Week on February 13 and G League Player of the month for March.{{cite web|url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/chris-clemons-040522/|title=Chris Clemons Named NBA G League Player Of The Month|accessdate=May 7, 2022|date=April 5, 2022|work=[[NBA.com]]}} Clemons joined the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612737/hawks |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} ===Windy City Bulls (2022)=== On September 29, 2022, Clemons' returning player rights were traded by the Celtics to the [[Windy City Bulls]]. On October 13, he signed a contract with the Bulls.{{cite web|url=https://ontapsportsnet.com/bulls/windy-city-bulls-training-camp-roster-released-chicago-bulls-two-way-players|website=ontapsportsnet.com|title=Windy City Bulls Finalize Training Camp Roster|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=October 23, 2022}} On November 23, Clemons was bought out by the Bulls. ===Xinjiang Flying Tigers (2022–2023)=== In November 2022, Clemons signed with the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite web|first=Dario|last=Skerletic|title=Chris Clemons to sign with Xinjiang|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/chris-clemons-to-sign-with-xinjiang/|website=Sportando.basketball|date=November 8, 2022|access-date=December 17, 2023}} ===Return to Windy City (2023–2024)=== On November 2, 2023, Clemons rejoined the [[Windy City Bulls]].{{cite web|title=Windy City Bulls Announce 2023 Training Camp Roster|url=https://windycity.gleague.nba.com/news/the-windy-city-bulls-announce-2023-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=November 2, 2023|access-date=November 9, 2023}} However, he was waived on February 1, 2024.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Windy City Bulls Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Windy-City-Bulls/44/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=February 2, 2024}} ===SLUC Nancy (2024–2025)=== On February 17, 2024, Clemons signed with [[SLUC Nancy Basket|SLUC Nancy]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{cite web|title=CHRIS CLEMONS AU SLUC NANCY BASKET!|url=https://sluc-basket.fr/actualites-du-club/chris-clemons-au-sluc-nancy-basket.html|website=SLUC-Basket.fr|date=February 17, 2024|access-date=February 17, 2024|language=French}} ===Baskets Oldenburg (2025–2026)=== On July 21, 2025, he signed with [[EWE Baskets Oldenburg]] in the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL).{{Cite web|url=https://ewe-baskets.de/news/verpflichtung-clemons.html|title=Neuer Spielmacher mit NBA-Erfahrung: Chris Clemons verstärkt EWE Baskets|date=July 21, more than any other BBL player in the previous 30 years.{{Cite web|url=https://ewe-baskets.de/gametime/spielberichte/ewe-baskets-oldenburg-vet-concept-gladiators-trier10885.html|title=52 Punkte! Clemons-Show mit Club-Rekord trägt zum ersten BBL-Sieg|date=October 24, 2025|website=ewe-baskets.de|publisher=|language=de|access-date=October 25, 2025}}{{Cite
